title: A Real-Time Communication Framework for Distributed Wearable Human Activity Recognition
content: Real-time systems for Human Activity Recognition (HAR) with multiple wearable sensors require not only accurate classification models, but also an inference architecture capable of distributing computation, reducing communication payload, and maintaining temporal consistency across asynchronous sensor streams. This paper presents a real-time distributed HAR framework in which each wearable sensor is associated with a local embedded node responsible for data acquisition, window segmentation, preprocessing, and neural inference. Instead of transmitting raw inertial windows to a central processor, each local node transmits a timestamped softmax probability vector representing its local activity estimate. A central fusion node receives the local probability messages, applies approximate timestamp-based synchronization, and generates the final activity prediction through probability-level fusion. The framework was evaluated during real-time experiments involving six activities, five wearable inertial sensors, and distributed embedded nodes. The system achieved 95.86% global accuracy, a macro F1-score of 95.84%, a mean end-to-end latency of 33.96 ms, and a mean synchronization span of 13.787 ms, demonstrating feasible real-time distributed HAR under live communication and synchronization constraints.
